text:
Maya (Product): Quick sync — we need to reconcile the customer asks for the Console observability roadmap. They want: per-route cost breakdown, trace->cost linking, better error analytics (fingerprinting + RCA tags), and a dashboard kit for finance. We have limited ENG bandwidth this quarter. Can we propose a conservative MVP that satisfies customers without blowing scope?

Jordan (Eng-ML): +1. My gut: prioritize hot-path features. If we do per-route cost for the top 5 routes and provide a single-click link from cost row -> trace view, that's a lot of customer value with much less infra work.

Sam (Eng-SRE): Tracing hooks: small change to request metadata to carry trace_id/cost_tag, sampling config tweak. Est ~2 sprints to ship hooks + storage backfill. Per-invocation exact cost is harder — token accounting + batching + KV cache interactions.

Ellie (Support): From field: enterprise beta customers (finance teams) insist on "accurate" per-invocation cost for chargebacks. They won't accept coarse estimates as a GA ask. For preview it's okay.

Maya (Product): Proposal to negotiate: 
- Preview (Q3): hosted = estimated per-route cost (95% correlated), dashboards showing aggregated route costs, trace linking for sampled traces.
- GA (Q4): dedicated/private = exact per-invocation attribution and exportable CSVs for finance.
Can Eng live with that split?

Jordan (Eng-ML): Split makes sense product-wise. Implementation note: estimated cost requires token accounting + model profile heuristics — that's relatively lightweight. Exact attribution requires integrating with the billing pipeline and ensuring deterministic token counts across caches.

Sam (Eng-SRE): For exact attribution we need to: 
1) propagate per-request token delta from model runtime,
2) persist per-request metrics atomically (cost+trace id),
3) add a nightly reconcile job to validate billing.
Estimate: 3 sprints for end-to-end on Dedicated infra.

Ellie (Support): Customers will accept "Preview" if we label it clearly and provide a migration path to exact metrics for Dedicated. Also need an error-analytics view that surfaces "top 20 fingerprints" and links to traces.

Maya (Product): Draft acceptance criteria for Preview (hosted):
```
- Dashboards: route-level cost widget (top 10 routes), time-range filter, export CSV (aggregate).
- Cost->Trace linking: click on a route row -> opens trace list filtered by route + example sampled trace.
- Error analytics: fingerprint list + count + sample trace per fingerprint.
- Documentation: clear note that hosted cost is estimated; accuracy metric shown (corr coeff vs dedicated baseline).
- UX: finance template dashboard saved and shareable.
```
If we meet these, we can call it Preview and collect feedback.

Jordan (Eng-ML): Minor ask: include confidence interval for estimates and a metric endpoint so customers can pull raw per-route aggregates (not per-invocation). That reduces support tickets.

Sam (Eng-SRE): Implementation risk: the reconcile job for exact billing has edge cases with cache warm/cold. We'll need test harness and synthetic traffic to validate. Flagging for infra budget.

Maya (Product): Trade decision: we accept some inaccuracy in hosted preview to move faster. Dedicated customers buying SLAs get exact. That should satisfy sales. Ellie, can you confirm a small set of customers we show Preview to?

Ellie (Support): Yes — Eileen Corp and NovaApps are ok with Preview labelled clearly. I'll coordinate release notes and a short FAQ for finance teams.

jira-bot: Created ticket PROD-2489: "obs: Preview per-route cost + trace linking" assigned to eng-ml, eng-sre, priority P2. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROD-2489

Maya (Product): Next steps:
- Jordan/Sam: scope tech spikes for sampling + token-accounting (due EOD Fri).
- Ellie: draft preview messaging and customer list.
- I'll prepare a proposal for PM sync Friday to get buy-in from GTM and Eng leadership.

Jordan (Eng-ML): I'll post a short RFC with perf/estimate approach after the spike.

Sam (Eng-SRE): I'll size the reconcile job and outline test harness.

Maya (Product): Thanks — sounds like a workable compromise. We'll iterate based on the spike results. :thumbsup:
